elements.quote: Methods A living systematic review.
elements.reason: The abstract text explicitly identifies the report as a “living systematic review.”
No explicit statement of the main objective or review question is provided in the retrieved abstract evidence.

elements.quote: Studies including at least 100 people with confirmed or clinically suspected COVID-­ 19 at 12 weeks or more post onset were included.
elements.reason: The retrieved abstract evidence states a key inclusion criterion, but it does not provide the main exclusion criteria as required.

elements.quote: Medline, CINAHL (EBSCO), Global Health (Ovid), WHO Global Research on COVID-­ 19 database, LitCovid and Google Scholar were searched till 17 March 2021.
elements.reason: The abstract provides the information sources searched and the date when searching was last completed (“till 17 March 2021”).

elements.quote: Risk of bias was assessed using the tool produced by Hoy et al .
elements.reason: The abstract reports the method/tool used to assess risk of bias.

elements.quote: Results were analysed using descriptive statistics and meta-­ analyses to estimate prevalence.
elements.reason: The abstract describes the methods used to present/summarize and synthesize results (descriptive statistics and meta-analyses).
The retrieved abstract evidence does not report the total number of included studies and participants, nor does it summarize relevant study characteristics.
The retrieved abstract evidence does not present results for the main outcomes (e.g., number of included studies/participants per outcome).

The retrieved abstract evidence mentions that meta-analyses were used, but it does not provide evidence about reporting a summary estimate with confidence/credible intervals in the abstract; therefore this conditional item cannot be verified from the retrieved abstract content.
No abstract evidence is provided that groups were compared in a way that would require reporting direction of effect and which group is favored.
The retrieved abstract evidence does not include a brief summary of important limitations of the included evidence.
The retrieved abstract evidence does not provide a general interpretation of results or their important implications.
No primary source of funding for the review is reported in the retrieved abstract evidence.
Although PROSPERO registration is mentioned elsewhere in retrieved evidence, the abstract evidence provided does not include the register name and registration number.

elements.quote: ► Long COVID is a heterogeneous condition with an uncertain prevalence, for which there is currently no precise case definition.
elements.reason: The evidence describes the current state of knowledge (heterogeneity) and an important uncertainty (uncertain prevalence/no precise case definition).

elements.quote: Background While it is now apparent clinical sequelae (long COVID) may persist after acute COVID-19, their nature, frequency and aetiology are poorly characterised. This study aims to regularly synthesise evidence on long COVID characteristics, to help inform clinical management, rehabilitation strategies and interventional studies to improve long-­ term outcomes.
elements.reason: The need and importance of conducting the review are explicitly explained in relation to poorly characterised nature/frequency/aetiology and its purpose to inform management and outcomes.

elements.quote: Systematic reviews conducted early during the COVID-­ 19 pandemic soon became redundant due to the rapidity with which new research was released.
elements.reason: The evidence explains that earlier systematic reviews became redundant, but it does not identify and cite specific previous systematic reviews or describe the current review as an update/replication with explicit citations to prior reviews.

The retrieved evidence describes a living systematic review to synthesise evidence on symptoms/characteristics (not intervention effects), so a proposed mechanism of action for an intervention is not applicable for this criterion.
The retrieved evidence does not describe a complex intervention or delivery context requiring a logic model; therefore this criterion is not applicable based on the available information.

elements.quote: This study aims to regularly synthesise evidence on long COVID characteristics, to help inform clinical management, rehabilitation strategies and interventional studies to improve long-­ term outcomes.
elements.reason: An objective is stated (“aims to regularly synthesise evidence on long COVID characteristics”), but the evidence provided does not show that the objective(s) or question(s) are explicitly stated using a relevant question-formulation framework.
The retrieved evidence does not indicate this review is an intervention-effects review with planned comparisons requiring PICO (or a variant).

elements.quote: Peer-­ reviewed studies were considered eligible if they included at least 100 people with laboratory confirmed and/or clinically diagnosed COVID-­ 19. Without a clear, internationally agreed case definition, we included studies that reported symptoms or outcomes assessed at 12 or more weeks post COVID-­ 19 onset.
elements.reason: The eligibility criteria specify key study characteristics used for inclusion: required participant number (≥100), case ascertainment (laboratory confirmed/clinically diagnosed COVID-19), and follow-up duration threshold (≥12 weeks post onset).

elements.quote: We identified 6459 studies, of which 39 met the inclusion criteria (online supplemental file 3), all of which were published in English.
elements.reason: Report-characteristic eligibility is partially specified (language: English). However, the evidence provided does not clearly specify dissemination year criteria or publication/report status criteria as part of eligibility.
No evidence is provided describing a distinction between exclusions where outcomes were not measured versus where outcome results were not reported.

elements.quote: We presented symptom proportions by different settings, as presented in the individual studies: hospitalised, non-­ hospitalised or a mix of both populations if no subset data were available. Symptoms were broadly grouped into physiological clusters through discussion with clinicians.
elements.reason: The evidence specifies grouping used in synthesis (settings: hospitalised vs non-hospitalised vs mix; physiological clusters). However, it does not explicitly link these groups to the comparisons defined in the review objectives.

elements.quote: Studies were excluded if they included fewer than 100 participants, to avoid small study effects, 18 or the follow-­ up was unclear or less than 12 weeks post onset.
elements.reason: Rationale is provided for the participant-size restriction (to avoid small study effects). A rationale for other notable restrictions (e.g., excluding unclear follow-up or <12 weeks) is not explicitly stated in the provided evidence.

elements.quote: WHO Global Research Database on COVID-­ 19 and LitCovid from 1 January 2020 to 17 March 2021. Additionally, we searched Google Scholar on 17 March 2021
elements.reason: The last search/consultation date is reported for at least the listed databases/repositories and explicitly for Google Scholar (17 March 2021).

elements.quote: The following databases were searched: Medline and CINAHL (EBSCO), Global Health (Ovid), WHO Global Research Database on COVID-­ 19 and LitCovid from 1 January 2020 to 17 March 2021.
elements.reason: Names and coverage dates are provided for the bibliographic databases, and platform/interface is provided for Medline/CINAHL (EBSCO) and Global Health (Ovid); however, an interface/platform is not reported for WHO Global Research Database on COVID-19 and LitCovid.

elements.quote: The following databases were searched: Medline and CINAHL (EBSCO), Global Health (Ovid), WHO Global Research Database on COVID-­ 19 and LitCovid from 1 January 2020 to 17 March 2021.
elements.reason: For online repositories (WHO Global Research Database on COVID-19 and LitCovid), both the repository names and the date range (1 January 2020 to 17 March 2021) are reported.

elements.quote: Additionally, we searched Google Scholar on 17 March 2021, screening the first 500 titles.
elements.reason: The online source name (Google Scholar) and the search date are reported, but no URL is provided.
No organisations or manufacturers contacted to identify studies are reported in the retrieved evidence.
No types of individuals contacted to identify studies are reported in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: A 'backwards' snowball search was conducted of the references of systematic reviews.
elements.reason: The types of reference lists examined are specified as the references of systematic reviews and that the approach was backwards; however, no additional detail on which other types of reference lists were examined is given.
No seed reports, citation index/platform, or search date for forward/backward citation searching is reported in the retrieved evidence.
No journals or conference proceedings consulted (including source names, dates covered, or search methods) are reported in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: Full search terms are included in online supplemental file 1.
elements.reason: The manuscript indicates that full search terms are provided in an online supplemental file, but the retrieved evidence does not show the complete search strategy as actually run for each database/register/website within the report itself.

The retrieved evidence describes which databases were searched and that search terms are designed to “cast a wide net,” but it does not report any search limits or their justification by reference to eligibility criteria.
No published search approaches or filters are cited, nor any adaptations to published strategies described, in the retrieved evidence.
The retrieved evidence does not mention any natural-language processing or text-analysis tools used to identify or refine search terms.
Although Google Translate is mentioned for translating non-English articles, the retrieved evidence does not specify tools used to translate search strings between sources.
No validation of the search strategy (process or validation studies) is described in the retrieved evidence.
The retrieved evidence does not report any peer review of the search strategy (e.g., PRESS) or related process/tool.
The retrieved evidence does not describe whether the search structure was based on PICO, nor (if not) the final conceptual structure and explorations used to develop it.

elements.quote: Screening was performed independently by two systematic reviewers.
elements.reason: Reports the number of reviewers (two) for screening, but does not specify the number of reviewers screening records versus full reports at each screening stage.

elements.quote: Screening was performed independently by two systematic reviewers.
elements.reason: Explicitly states independent screening by two systematic reviewers.

elements.quote: Any disagreements were resolved via consensus or a third reviewer.
elements.reason: Describes the process for resolving screening disagreements.
No description found of processes used to obtain or confirm eligibility information from study investigators.

elements.quote: Non-­ English articles were translated using Google Translate and assessed by a systematic reviewer with good knowledge of the language.
elements.reason: Specifies the method used to translate non-English articles for eligibility assessment.

elements.quote: The data were managed using the review software Rayyan.
elements.reason: Mentions an automation/review management tool (Rayyan) but does not describe how automation was integrated into the selection process (e.g., automation features used).
No externally derived classifiers, versions/references, or removal of records before screening are described.

elements.quote: Data extraction was performed by one systematic reviewer and checked by a second reviewer.
elements.reason: The manuscript reports that data extraction was done by one reviewer and checked by a second (i.e., the number of reviewers involved per report).

elements.quote: Data extraction was performed by one systematic reviewer and checked by a second reviewer.
elements.reason: It specifies the number and roles (one reviewer plus a second checking reviewer) but does not explicitly state whether data collectors worked independently.

elements.quote: Non-­ English articles were translated using Google Translate and assessed by a systematic reviewer with good knowledge of the language.
elements.reason: The method for translating non-English articles for the review/data collection process is reported, including that translation was done with Google Translate and assessed by a reviewer.

elements.quote: Without a clear, internationally agreed case definition, we included studies that reported symptoms or outcomes assessed at 12 or more weeks post COVID-­ 19 onset.

The evidence does not state whether all compatible results within each outcome domain were sought.

elements.quote: Data extracted included study design, population characteristics, outcomes, prevalence, duration of symptoms and risk factors.
elements.reason: The review reports that the data extraction included several variables, but the evidence does not show that all other sought variables are comprehensively listed and defined (e.g., definitions and any additional variables such as funding sources are not provided in the retrieved text).

elements.quote: A data extraction template informed by a previous review 20 was reviewed, updated and piloted before being finalised.
elements.reason: A data extraction template (informed by a previous review) is described, but the evidence does not clearly state this as the specific tool used to determine which data items to collect, nor does it describe how it was used for item selection.

elements.quote: The included studies were assessed for risk of bias using the tool produced by Hoy et al 21 (online supplemental file 2).

elements.quote: This assessment checklist is a validated tool for assessing risk of bias in prevalence studies. The checklist has 10 domains for assessing risk of bias, used to calculate a cumulative overall risk of bias for the whole study.
elements.reason: It is stated that the tool has 10 domains, but the individual domains/components/items are not specified in the retrieved text.

elements.quote: The checklist has 10 domains for assessing risk of bias, used to calculate a cumulative overall risk of bias for the whole study.

No adaptations to the risk-of-bias tool are reported in the retrieved evidence.

No processes are described for obtaining or confirming risk-of-bias information from study investigators in the retrieved evidence.
No automation tools for risk-of-bias assessment are described in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: Proportion of symptoms and its 95% CIs were estimated using the exact method. 22 If there were two or more studies for each symptom, a meta-­ analysis was performed using a random intercept logistic regression model with Hartung-­ Knapp modification due to the heterogeneity and skewed sample sizes. 23 24
elements.reason: The effect metric used for synthesis/presentation is described as symptom proportions with 95% CIs, using an exact method and a logistic regression meta-analysis model, but it is not clearly specified for every outcome/outcome type.
No thresholds or ranges used to interpret effect size (and their rationale) are reported in the retrieved evidence.
The retrieved evidence does not describe methods for re-expressing synthesized results using another effect measure.

elements.quote: If there were two or more studies for each symptom, a meta-­ analysis was performed using a random intercept logistic regression model with Hartung-­ Knapp modification due to the heterogeneity and skewed sample sizes.
elements.reason: There is some rationale for the modelling approach (logistic regression with Hartung-Knapp due to heterogeneity/skew), but the retrieved evidence does not explicitly justify the choice of effect measure itself for synthesis/presentation.

elements.quote: Peer-­ reviewed studies were considered eligible if they included at least 100 people with laboratory confirmed and/or clinically diagnosed COVID-­ 19. Without a clear, internationally agreed case definition, we included studies that reported symptoms or outcomes assessed at 12 or more weeks post COVID-­ 19 onset.
elements.reason: The manuscript describes eligibility criteria for included studies, but the retrieved evidence does not clearly describe the processes used to decide which studies were eligible for each specific synthesis (e.g., comparing study intervention characteristics against planned groups for each synthesis).

elements.quote: Sensitivity analyses were conducted to examine the impact of high risk of bias studies and statistical methods, Freeman-­ Tukey double arcsine transformation using inverse variance meta-­ analysis, on the estimates.
elements.reason: The review describes at least one data-conversion/analysis preparation method (Freeman–Tukey double arcsine transformation for sensitivity analyses). However, the evidence does not clearly describe methods for handling missing summary statistics (e.g., missing data handling/conversion rules), which are also part of the criterion.

elements.quote: The data are presented using a combination of infographics, prepared by a design company (Design Science 29 ) and scientific tables to facilitate interpretation by different stakeholders, including non-­ specialists.
elements.reason: The evidence states that “scientific tables” are used to present data, but it does not describe the specific tabular structures or exactly what data fields/columns are included in the tables.

elements.quote: All analysis and data presentation were performed using metaprop 26 and ggplot2 27 in R (V.4.0.5) via RStudio (V.1.3.1093).
elements.reason: The evidence indicates graphical methods/tools used (ggplot2) and mentions infographics, but it does not describe the graphical methods for tabulating/visually displaying individual study vs synthesis results in sufficient detail. Visual infographic evidence is also present (Figure 5/6) but no accompanying descriptive methods are provided here.

elements.quote: Symptoms were broadly grouped into physiological clusters through discussion with clinicians.
elements.reason: The basis for grouping/order of symptoms within visual/tabular presentations is explicitly reported as physiological clusters determined via clinician discussion.
No rationale is reported for using non-standard graphs/visual displays.

elements.quote: All analysis and data presentation were performed using metaprop 26 and ggplot2 27 in R (V.4.0.5) via RStudio (V.1.3.1093). 28
elements.reason: Reports software/packages and versions used for analysis and data presentation.

elements.quote: The remaining studies include single symptoms or imaging and diagnostics and are presented narratively.
elements.reason: An alternative to meta-analysis (narrative presentation) is described, but no explicit rationale is provided for when/how meta-analysis was not possible.

elements.quote: If there were two or more studies for each symptom, a meta-­ analysis was performed using a random intercept logistic regression model with Hartung-­ Knapp modification due to the heterogeneity and skewed sample sizes.
elements.reason: For meta-analysis, the model is specified and the rationale (heterogeneity and skewed sample sizes) is given.

elements.quote: Proportion of symptoms and its 95% CIs were estimated using the exact method. 22 If there were two or more studies for each symptom, a meta-­ analysis was performed using a random intercept logistic regression model with Hartung-­ Knapp modification due to the heterogeneity and skewed sample sizes.
elements.reason: Reports the statistical approach used for estimating proportions/95% CIs and for meta-analysis (random intercept logistic regression with Hartung–Knapp modification).

elements.quote: Heterogeneity between estimates was assessed using the I 2 statistic.
elements.reason: States the method used to identify/quantify statistical heterogeneity (I²).
No between-study variance estimator for random-effects meta-analysis is reported in the available evidence.

elements.quote: Proportion of symptoms and its 95% CIs were estimated using the exact method.
elements.reason: 95% confidence intervals are described as using the exact method, but it is not clearly tied to the random-effects meta-analysis implementation for summary effects.
Other random-effects implementation details are not reported in the available evidence.
No Bayesian meta-analysis is described in the available evidence, so prior distributions cannot be assessed.
No methods are reported for accounting for statistical dependency among multiple estimates from the same study.
No planned syntheses judged impossible or inappropriate (and reasons) are reported in the available evidence.

elements.quote: Additional subgroup analysis was conducted to explore the modification of the following factors on proportion of symptoms: hospitalisation, settings, continents and follow-­ up timing. We also conducted meta-­ regression analysis on the percentage of females and intensive care unit (ICU) patients where there were more than 10 studies for the symptom.
elements.reason: The methods used to explore heterogeneity included subgroup analysis and meta-regression.

elements.quote: Additional subgroup analysis was conducted to explore the modification of the following factors on proportion of symptoms: hospitalisation, settings, continents and follow-­ up timing.
elements.reason: Factors for subgroup analysis are reported, but factor levels and expected direction of effect modification are not described in the retrieved evidence.
The retrieved evidence describes subgroup analysis and meta-regression, but does not specify whether analyses used study-level variables, within-study contrasts, or both.
The retrieved evidence states subgroup analyses were conducted, but does not describe the methods used to compare subgroup effects.
No informal methods for exploring heterogeneity are described for situations where meta-analysis was unsuitable.
The retrieved evidence does not identify whether any heterogeneity analyses were not pre-specified.

elements.quote: Sensitivity analyses were conducted to examine the impact of high risk of bias studies and statistical methods, Freeman-­ Tukey double arcsine transformation using inverse variance meta-­ analysis, on the estimates.
elements.reason: The report states that sensitivity analyses were conducted (high risk of bias studies and the Freeman–Tukey double arcsine transformation), but it does not provide details of every sensitivity analysis performed beyond these examples.
The evidence does not identify which (if any) sensitivity analyses were not pre-specified.

elements.quote: The included studies were assessed for risk of bias using the tool produced by Hoy et al 21 (online supplemental file 2). This assessment checklist is a validated tool for assessing risk of bias in prevalence studies. The checklist has 10 domains for assessing risk of bias, used to calculate a cumulative overall risk of bias for the whole study.
elements.reason: The review reports the overall risk-of-bias tool used, but the evidence does not describe methods specifically for assessing risk of bias due to missing results arising from reporting biases.

elements.quote: The checklist has 10 domains for assessing risk of bias, used to calculate a cumulative overall risk of bias for the whole study.
elements.reason: For the existing Hoy et al tool, the assessed domains (10 domains) and the process for an overall judgement (cumulative overall risk of bias for the whole study) are described.
No information is provided about any adaptations made to the Hoy et al reporting-bias tool.
There is no description of any newly developed reporting-bias tool or its public availability.
The evidence does not report the number of reviewers, their independence, or disagreement-resolution procedures for the reporting-bias/risk-of-bias assessment.
No processes are described for obtaining or confirming relevant information from study investigators.
No automation tools for reporting-bias assessment (including use, training, performance, or validation) are described.

No factors/criteria used to assess certainty (or confidence) for each outcome are reported in the retrieved evidence.
No decision rules for deriving an overall certainty level, or interpretation of each level, are reported in the retrieved evidence.
The retrieved evidence does not describe any certainty-assessment method, so no review-specific certainty considerations/thresholds/rationales can be identified.
Because no certainty-assessment system is described in the retrieved evidence, there is no adaptation of an existing certainty system to report.

The retrieved evidence does not describe any certainty-assessment process, so no processes for obtaining/confirming relevant information from investigators for certainty assessment are reported.
No automation tools are mentioned for certainty assessment; the retrieved evidence only discusses risk-of-bias assessment and other review processes.

No numbers are reported for reports sought, not retrieved, assessed for eligibility, or excluded with primary reasons.

No data are reported on ongoing studies and associated reports.

elements.quote: Table 1 presents the included study characteristics.

elements.quote: Proportion of symptoms and its 95% CIs were estimated using the exact method.

elements.quote: 7 A deeper understanding of long COVID is currently prevented by the limitations of the published literature. The studies included in our review were highly heterogeneous due to differences in their study designs, settings, populations, follow-­ up time and symptom ascertainment methods. In addition, studies used inconsistent terminology describing symptoms and limited details and stratification on pre-­ existing comorbidities, the severity of COVID-­ 19 and treatment methods. This inconsistency and limited reporting partly explain the high degree of variability observed. The lack of case-control studies prevent a direct attribution of symptoms solely to COVID-­ 19; larger prospective studies with matched control groups are needed.
